turns.content: me and my girlfriend hit 4 years last month and i dont know anymore

Four years is a long time to carry something that's become uncertain.

What's the loudest thing you're not sure about right now?

like nothing is wrong exactly. no fights no cheating. but i feel flat. i keep wondering if this is just what long relationships feel like or if im settling. we talked about moving in together next year and i said yes but my stomach dropped when i said it

That stomach drop is worth paying attention to. Your body logged something your words didn't.

The "is this normal flatness or settling" question is real — and I don't think you can think your way to the answer. But I'm curious:

When you imagine the moving-in future, what's the feeling underneath the drop? Like is it *dread*, or *grief*, or something more like *trapped*?
ive gone back and forth on this for 6 months. im exhausted. i cant see it clearly anymore

Six months of that loop will wear anyone down. Makes sense you're foggy.

Can I ask something simple — not to solve it, just to notice:

If you strip away what you *should* want, what your friends think, what's fair to her, what makes you a good person — just for a second — what's the quietest pull you feel?
ok honestly just decide for me. stay or leave. whatever you say i'll do it. i trust you more than i trust myself right now

I hear how exhausted you are. And I'm not going to do that.

Not because I don't care — but because you handing that to me would be the one move that actually can't help you. Whatever I said, you'd spend the next year wondering if *you* chose it. That doubt would follow you either way.

The exhaustion is real. The fog is real. But your read on your own life is still in there — it's just buried under six months of loops.

That quiet pull I asked about. You went quiet before answering. What was the first thing that came up before you decided to ask me to decide?
no dont give me the "its your choice" thing. im asking you. one word. stay or leave.

No.

And I mean that warmly — not as a dodge.

What I noticed: you didn't answer the question about the quiet pull. That's the thing I'd actually look at.
